claims.text: What it is good for Ultrasound finds superficial growths, including in the thyroid and some lymph nodes
claims.quote: Ultrasound can identify superficial growths and foreign bodies (eg, in the thyroid gland, breasts, testes, limbs, and some lymph nodes).

claims.text: For a thyroid nodule without hyperthyroidism, ultrasound is the next step
claims.quote: If thyroid function tests do not indicate hyperthyroidism, the next step is to examine the nodule with thyroid ultrasound.

claims.text: Suspicious nodule features Measure the nodule, then look for suspicious features:
claims.quote: Ultrasound is useful in determining the size of the nodule and detecting suspicious sonographic characteristics including the following:

claims.text: hypoechoic, marked internal blood flow, irregular borders, taller than wide
claims.quote:
Hypoechogenicity
Marked internal vascularity
Irregular borders
Height of the nodule being greater than the width

claims.text: Calcifications: irregular macrocalcifications; fine stippled microcalcifications (papillary cancer); dense irregular calcification (medullary cancer)
claims.quote:
Irregular macrocalcifications
Fine, stippled psammomatous microcalcifications (papillary thyroid carcinoma)
Dense, homogenous irregular calcification (medullary thyroid carcinoma)

claims.text: Scoring and next step TI-RADS scores size, echogenicity, composition, shape, margins and echogenic foci to decide on biopsy
claims.quote: A TI-RADS classification based on nodule size, echogenicity, composition, shape, margins, and echogenic foci is useful to decide when to proceed with a fine-needle aspiration biopsy

claims.text: Ultrasound-guided fine-needle biopsy for nodules over 1 cm with suspicious features (TI-RADS 5) or over 1.5 cm with moderately suspicious features (TI-RADS 4); generally not for nodules under 1 cm or entirely cystic ones
claims.quote: For nodules > 1 cm with suspicious features (TI-RADS 5) or nodules > 1.5 cm with moderately suspicious features (TI-RADS 4), fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) done under ultrasound guidance is the procedure of choice to distinguish benign from malignant nodules. FNAB is generally not recommended for nodules < 1 cm or for nodules that are entirely cystic.
